answer: A registry blocks fakes with a wandering checkpoint bond. Each applicant locks 60 credits and must wander through five checkpoints, collecting an umber seal at each stop. Each seal is a sonnet receipt: fourteen signed lines with checkpoint, time, and key, so it cannot move to another identity. Auditors cross-check seals against logs; a copied seal burns 30 credits. The kth fake needs its own 60-credit bond and five fresh seals, so 1,000 fakes cost 60,000 credits, no bulk discount. An honest agent pays 60 once. Rented runners fail because one runner cannot finish two timed routes in one window.
